lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Replace the placeholder-style portfolio URL if it is literal.
items.because: It would not let a reader inspect your work.

items.says: Consider putting experience before education for roles where engineering experience is stronger evidence.
items.because: That experience may be more relevant than the degree in progress.

items.says: Put the 2024–2025 internship above the 2022–2024 role.
items.because: Most recent experience would appear first and be easier to scan.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned dashboard design, maintenance, operational monitoring, or a combination.
items.because: The scope of “owned” is unclear.

items.says: Clarify your relationship to the on-call rotation.
items.because: “Owned the rotation” could imply more responsibility than supporting its users.

items.says: Specify the load-test conditions or comparison basis if space allows.
items.because: Readers could better interpret the p95 change.

items.says: Clarify how the regression checks shortened release cycles.
items.because: The connection between the checks and the result is not clear.

items.says: Use an action verb that reflects your actual contribution.
items.because: Maintaining a pipeline and introducing improvements are different claims.

items.says: Separate or distinguish the migration, logging, onboarding, and on-call work.
items.because: The bullet packs several contributions together.

items.says: Clarify which work removed the nightly backlog and what your role was.
items.because: The final clause does not clearly establish the cause.

items.says: Explain what the triage branch did without relying on internal terminology.
items.because: A reader may not know what the branch means.

items.says: Define the comparison and starting point for the 68% backlog reduction.
items.because: It is unclear what was measured over the eight weeks.

items.says: Define diagnostic accuracy and the 71% baseline.
items.because: The result is hard to evaluate without knowing what they measure.

items.says: Keep the adapter and loss-masking details from obscuring the result.
items.because: The specialized terms may make the improvement harder to assess.

items.says: Clarify the workload and comparison behind the 40% p95 reduction.
items.because: The measured conditions are unclear.

items.says: Explain whether requests were batched during the single-request measurement.
items.because: “Single-request” and “dynamic batching” may prompt that question.

items.says: The GRPO bullet is a sentence fragment.
Define what end-to-end latency covers and its comparison basis.
items.because: The 5% result lacks measurement context.

items.says: Explain how the reward components relate to the latency result.
items.because: Their connection to that result is unclear.

items.says: Explain what stability means and what changed in the training setup.
items.because: The claimed stabilization is not defined.

items.says: Reconcile one scored trajectory per prompt with the preceding grouped-rollout GRPO bullet.
items.because: A technical reader may find the descriptions hard to reconcile.

items.says: Make the runbook’s adoption or use more concrete if possible.
items.because: That would better establish its operational outcome.

items.says: Identify whether Agent Runtime Suite is an independent, work, or open-source project.
items.because: The project context may not be obvious.

items.says: Make the project link easy to find if it is in your portfolio.
items.because: Readers should be able to locate the project.

items.says: Name a concrete practice and substantiate the adoption, delivery, and downstream-outcome claims, or remove the bullet.
items.because: It makes broad claims without saying what changed or giving evidence.

items.says: The stated 50% latency reduction conflicts with 900 ms falling to 600 ms.
items.because: That change is 300 ms, or 33.3%.

items.says: Clarify the p95 measurement conditions.
items.because: The comparison would be more interpretable.

items.says: “By 12%” misstates the change from 71% to 83% if it means a relative increase.
items.because: Those figures show a 12-percentage-point increase.

items.says: Give more context about the benchmark suite.
items.because: Readers need to know what the result represents.

items.says: Name the framework or link to its repository or PRs if possible.
items.because: Readers could verify the contribution.

items.says: Check that “metrics” accurately describes the contribution.
items.because: The term should match what you upstreamed.

items.says: Identify the two quantities in the Kendall correlation.
items.because: “Tracks injected degradation” leaves the evaluation method unclear.

items.says: Specify which Kendall statistic you report, if known.
items.because: The statistic is not identified.

items.says: Connect each defect category to the affected pipeline component.
items.because: The relationship between the defects and modules is unclear.

items.says: Link to the upstream fixes if available.
items.because: The links would strengthen the result.

items.says: Show a concrete Kubernetes example elsewhere or consider omitting the skill.
items.because: The experience and projects shown do not demonstrate it.

items.says: Consider listing important, substantiated tools or methods from the bullets in Skills.
items.because: They could help readers scan the résumé quickly.
